title: Finite coefficient extension and mixed realization coherence
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Module sheaves, sheaf tensor products, derived categories and cohomology are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,A)$ for the completed integral category including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and $Q:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=\mathcal C_X[1/\varpi]$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. A rational module sheaf is constructible when on a finite locally closed stratification it is pro-etale locally finite free [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Write $F_X(K)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$ and $J_X(QK)=F_X(K)$, $J_X(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$ for the functor specified in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with arbitrary ramification, put $A_L=\mathcal O_L$, $B_{L,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_L/\varpi_L^n)_X$ and $L_X=B_{L,X}[1/\varpi_L]$, and define $J_{L,X}$ by the same formulas. For raw scalar extension $T_{L/E}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], there is a natural isomorphism
$$\theta_{L/E,X}:J_{L,X}T_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}(L_X\otimes^L_{E_X}-)J_{E,X}.$$
It is the balanced identification through $L_X\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$ on an integral representative, using the actual integral functor $B_{L,X}\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$ and the continuous coefficient maps of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations]. On K-flat representatives the comparison flattens $(l\otimes b)\otimes k$ to $lb\otimes k$, with inverse inserting $1$; it respects raw fractions since every nonzero scalar of $E$ becomes invertible in $L$. For $E\subset L\subset M$ its successive-extension diagram commutes with the specified raw scalar associators: both routes flatten $m\otimes l\otimes k$ to $ml\otimes k$; the identity and four-field pentagon diagrams commute as well. For any scheme map $g:X'\to X$ between schemes satisfying the hypotheses, the square comparing $\theta$ and the specific $\alpha_g$ of [lem-per-rational-realization-pullback-comparison] commutes with the scalar/pullback comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The integral coefficient square is the finite-quotient-normalized one; after localization the balanced map on both routes sends $l'\otimes b'\otimes k$ to $l'b'\otimes g^{-1}k$. These equalities hold with the completion units, ambient pullback composition comparisons and all successive coefficient associators, using [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. No pair-category descent or unramified-extension assumption is used.

proof.text: For $W=X,X'$, abbreviate $R_W=B_{E,W}$, $S_W=B_{L,W}$ and $C_W=S_W\otimes^L_{R_W}-$. The integral inclusion $i_W:R_W\to S_W$ has $n$-th projection $(\iota_n)_W\pi^E_n$, where $\iota_n:A/\varpi_E^n\to A_L/\varpi_L^n$ is induced by inclusion. For $g:X'\to X$, the two maps $g^{-1}R_X\to S_{X'}$ agree: after projection to $(A_L/\varpi_L^n)_{X'}$ both are the constant-sheaf coefficient map after the pulled-back $E$-quotient projection. Equality into the inverse limit proves the integral coefficient square. Under continuous-coefficient realization this says that precomposition with the geometric projection commutes with postcomposition by the field inclusion. Localization gives the same square for $E_W\to L_W$, preserving the coefficient units. In particular every nonzero constant of $E$ has inverse its constant reciprocal in $L_W$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; explicit finite-projection coefficient-square calculation

proof.text:
Let $K\in\mathcal C_X$. The integral representative of $T_{L/E}QK$ is $C_XK$, by the scalar-extension statement. Set $U_X(K)=L_X\otimes^L_{R_X}K$. Derived pullback composition on the identity underlying topos supplies natural isomorphisms
$$s_K:L_X\otimes^L_{S_X}(S_X\otimes^L_{R_X}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}U_X(K),\quad t_K:L_X\otimes^L_{E_X}(E_X\otimes^L_{R_X}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}U_X(K).$$
They use the coefficient maps from Step 1. To compute them, take a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$; both $S_X\otimes_{R_X}P$ and $E_X\otimes_{R_X}P$ remain flat-term K-flat over their new rings. Thus $s_K$ and $t_K$ are induced by $(l\otimes b)\otimes p\mapsto lb\otimes p$, and their inverses insert $1$. Define $\theta_{L/E,X,QK}=t_K^{-1}s_K$. The derived composition and monoidal comparisons ensure independence of the representative and naturality for all integral derived morphisms, not merely chain maps.

Pass to raw rational morphisms using the stated formulas for $J$ and $T$. For $f/\varpi_E^n$, naturality of Step 2 for $f$ can be multiplied by the central scalar $\varpi_E^{-n}$ on both sides, since Step 1 makes that scalar invertible in $L_X$. This gives naturality for $f/\varpi_E^n$. Explicitly, if $f/\varpi_E^n=h/\varpi_E^m$, then some $r\geq0$ kills $\varpi_E^mf-\varpi_E^nh$ after multiplication by $\varpi_E^r$; applying the integral functors and multiplying by $\varpi_E^{-r-m-n}$ gives equality of their localized images. Each component remains invertible, with inverse $s_K^{-1}t_K$. This proves the required natural isomorphism on the raw categories.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2); explicit calculation on the raw scalar-localized Hom groups

proof.text: For $E\subset L\subset M$, express both successive-extension routes using $s,t$ and the specified raw scalar associators. The intermediate $s^{-1}s$ and $t^{-1}t$ cancel. On the common K-flat tensor model the remaining maps both send $m\otimes l\otimes p$ to $ml\otimes p$. These are precisely the derived monoidal composition comparisons, so the equality holds in the derived category and on raw fractions by Step 3. For a fourth field and a scalar $n$ from it, every pentagon route sends $n\otimes m\otimes l\otimes p$ to $nml\otimes p$; associativity of ring multiplication proves their equality. For repeated fields the raw functor is literally the identity and these maps reduce to the multiplication unitors. Their unit equations follow by $1l=l=l1$.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); normalized tensor associators and units, explicit field-tower calculation

proof.text:
Write $\Lambda_{E,W}$ and $\Lambda_{L,W}$ for local derived-completion reflectors, with units $\eta_E,\eta_L$. The ringed Koszul-completion theorem supplies these reflectors and their universal unit property. They are the specified quotient completions, with the same units, by the constant/completed coefficient comparison. The sheaf $S_W$ is finite free over $R_W$ of rank $[L:E]$. The inclusion preserves the absolute value, and the DVR factorization of $\varpi_E$ in $\mathcal O_L$ is $u\varpi_L^e$ for a unit $u$ and $e\geq1$: its absolute value is strictly less than $1$. These are the hypotheses of finite-free completion transport. Consequently there is a unit-normalized natural isomorphism
$$\kappa_W:C_W\Lambda_{E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{L,W}C_W,\qquad \kappa_{W,N}C_W(\eta_{E,N})=\eta_{L,C_WN}.$$
It respects identity coefficients and successive scalar associators. This applies to ambient complexes before any constructibility restriction, and allows arbitrary positive ramification index.

source.place: Tag 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul), with Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.8.2 and the unit-normalized finite-free completion comparison

proof.text:
Put $P_{F,g}=B_{F,X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}B_{F,X}}g^{-1}(-)$ for $F=E,L$. Step 1 and ringed derived composition give the ordinary balanced comparison $\beta_g:C_{X'}P_{E,g}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{L,g}C_X$. On flat-term K-flat representatives both sides flatten to $S_{X'}\otimes_{g^{-1}R_X}g^{-1}P$; $s'\otimes r'\otimes p$ maps to $s'i_{X'}(r')\otimes p$. Apply the reflected-adjunction coefficient-square construction with $F_0=P_{E,g}$, $F_1=P_{L,g}$, $C_A=C_X$, $C_B=C_{X'}$ and its ordinary comparison $\delta=\beta_g^{-1}$. The ringed derived adjunctions are the canonical ones; their right adjoints preserve complete objects and have unit-normalized completion comparisons by the ringed-pushforward completion theorem. Step 5 supplies both $\kappa_T$. Thus all hypotheses of that construction hold. The resulting comparison is
$$\widehat\beta_g=\Lambda_{L,X'}(\beta_g)\kappa_{X',P_{E,g}K}:C_{X'}\widehat P_{E,g}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat P_{L,g}C_XK.$$
It is the finite-quotient-normalized scalar/pullback comparison used in the scalar-extension statement, with its indicated orientation.

source.place: Tag 0A0G (lemma-pushforward-commutes-with-derived-completion); unit-normalized reflected coefficient square, with sites-cohomology Tag 0D6D

proof.text:
The comparison in Step 6 respects the actual pullback completion units, rather than only the isomorphism classes of their sources and targets. Indeed the unit equation of Step 5 and naturality of $\eta_L$ give
$$\widehat\beta_{g,K}\,C_{X'}(\gamma_{E,g,K})=\Lambda_L(\beta_{g,K})\,\eta_{L,C_{X'}P_{E,g}K}=\gamma_{L,g,C_XK}\,\beta_{g,K}.$$
Here $\gamma_F$ is exactly ordinary pullback followed by its quotient-tower completion unit, by definition of completed pullback. The constant/completed coefficient comparison identifies that quotient unit with $\eta_F$. Thus the equation uses the finite quotient projections which fixed $\widehat P$; it does not choose an unrelated isomorphism. The pullback-realization statement makes both $\gamma$'s isomorphisms on the integral objects in question, and scalar extension carries these objects into the corresponding integral category.

source.place: Tag 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul); naturality of the completion unit and its finite-quotient normalization

proof.text: Compare the two mixed routes starting at $J_{L,X'}Q(C_{X'}\widehat P_{E,g}K)$. Precompose both by the isomorphism $J_{L,X'}Q(C_{X'}\gamma_{E,g,K})$. Step 7 then replaces $\widehat\beta_g$ followed by this map with $\gamma_L\beta_g$. By the specified formula for $\alpha_F$, composing $\alpha_F$ with $J_FQ(\gamma_F)$ cancels $J_FQ(\gamma_F^{-1})$ and leaves ordinary balanced localization. The inverse-image localization comparison preserves the localization units and identifies $g^{-1}E_X$ with $(g^{-1}R_X)[1/\varpi_E]$. All remaining maps are therefore maps of the common model $L_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}R_X}g^{-1}K$. Before flattening, a local tensor $l'\otimes b'\otimes p$ with $b'\in R_{X'}$ goes on either route to $l'i_{X'}(b')\otimes p$. Step 1 supplies exactly the equality of coefficient actions needed for balancing. Equality on these local generators gives equality of the chain maps on the K-flat models, hence of the derived maps. Cancel the precomposed isomorphism. This proves the square for the specific $\alpha_g$ and the scalar/pullback comparison in the statement.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; explicit mixed balanced-tensor square after cancellation of the specified completion units

proof.text: These equations also respect the ambient pullback composition comparisons and every successive scalar associator. The ordinary comparisons are the monoidal K-flat comparisons already used in Steps 2, 4 and 6. For a second geometric map, both ordinary composite routes are the same scalar-insertion and multiplication map after the canonical inverse-image compositor. The localization inverse-image isomorphisms satisfy precisely this composition equation. Reflection preserves pasting and identities for the unit-normalized coefficient squares, so the equation of Step 7 persists under both geometric composition and coefficient towers; the $\kappa$'s have the corresponding tower equation by Step 5. Substitute $\alpha_F=({\rm ordinary\ balancing})J_FQ(\gamma_F^{-1})$ in any resulting diagram: each adjacent completion-unit pair cancels, and the remaining diagram is the ordinary one just described. For three coefficient scalars its value is their product acting on the pulled-back representative, independent of parentheses. Finally Step 3 carries each equation to fraction morphisms. This proves all asserted identity, pentagon and mixed coherences without changing the coefficient category.
